display_name: Read what happened to a sent message by its message id
description: Use after a peer_send or peer_send_by_name returned a receipt that only says driver_scheduled or driver_not_needed, to learn what became of that message. Give the message_id the send returned. The result's delivery_state is one of read_by_recipient (the recipient's own inbox read returned the message), wake_typed (a wake notice was typed into the recipient's pane, the message not yet read), wake_attempt_running (the drive has not finished, read again in a few seconds), not_delivered (nothing reached the pane, for example because it was busy), channel_queued (the send reached the recipient's live channel, drive outcome driver_not_needed, so no wake notice was typed: queued on the recipient's live channel; delivery to the model is not observed; do not resend), no_driver_wake (the platform does not wake this recipient) or not_confirmed (no record exists). It also returns wake_attempt_outcome and wake_attempt_detail, evidence_source (wake_attempt_record, pickup_row or none), the durable pickup row (phase, reason, pending, attempts, version, checked_at), pickup_unavailable, and a fixed explanation. Read-only: it joins the finished wake attempt held in this process with the pickup row, writes nothing, never waits for a drive and builds no record of its own. The wake-attempt record lives in memory for the most recent 512 sends, so after a restart only the pickup row can answer; a Claude recipient's pickup row keeps a placeholder instead of the finished attempt, which reads as not_confirmed. The message itself is always stored: read_by_recipient proves the read, not that the work was done, and no state here is a reason to resend.
embedding_description: Check whether a message you already sent actually reached its recipient: look up the message id from the send receipt and read back whether a wake notice was typed into the pane, nothing was delivered because the pane was busy, or the recipient's inbox read returned it.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: message_id, delivery_state, wake_attempt_outcome, wake_attempt_detail, evidence_source, pickup (phase, reason, pending, attempts, version, checked_at, or null), pickup_unavailable, explanation.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Lead with delivery_state and give the explanation verbatim. not_delivered means nothing reached the recipient's pane: say so plainly and do not resend, because the message is stored and the recipient reads it at its next inbox read. wake_attempt_running means read again in a few seconds. channel_queued means the message was queued on the recipient's live channel and no wake notice was typed because none was needed (wake_attempt_outcome driver_not_needed): say that delivery to the model is not observed and do not resend. not_confirmed is neither a failure nor a delivery: say that delivery is not confirmed, and never present it as delivered. Never turn wake_typed or read_by_recipient into a claim that the recipient did the work. If pickup_unavailable is true, say the durable row could not be read and the answer rests on the in-process record alone.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A read of the in-process wake-attempt record and one filtered read of the delivery_pickup table by message_id; nothing is written and no drive is waited for.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_message_id: message_id was empty or absent, the only refusal. A message with no record anywhere is not an error: it returns delivery_state not_confirmed. A pickup row that could not be read does not fail the call: pickup_unavailable is true and the wake attempt alone answers. When the state service is not bound the pickup row is not read and pickup is null.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Pass the message_id from the send's own result. On not_confirmed do not resend: the message is stored and the recipient reads it at its next inbox read, so ask the recipient or read again later. If pickup_unavailable is true, read again; the platform log carries the failure.
